documents.title: OU Guidelines: Artificial Intelligence Usage
documents.summary: IT guidelines on responsible, transparent AI use across academic, research, clinical and business operations. They focus on data protection, human oversight of decisions about people, tool review and incident reporting, and send teaching questions to CETL.
documents.stance_why: The document sets no course-level AI stance. It permits AI 'to support decision-making, research, and operational efficiency', and for 'Teaching, Learning, and Academic Integrity' says 'Please refer to AI Guidance provided by the Center for Excellence in Teaching and Learning', so it hands the decision on.

units.why: The opening sentence states the purpose and scope of the guidelines ('used responsibly, ethically, and transparently across academic, research, and administrative functions'), which is an institution-wide framework preamble, so P56 with informs modality.
units.anchor: ensure that Generative AI and LLMs are used responsibly, ethically, and transparently

units.why: 'All AI use requires disclosure' is a blanket rule that AI use must be disclosed, addressed to everyone; P24 (disclose with submissions) is the nearest type although the sentence is cut off in the source.
units.anchor: All AI use requires disclosure, rigorous review, and safeguard

units.why: The overview permits AI for 'decision-making, research, and operational efficiency', an operational-use rule rather than a teaching rule, so P76 (administrative and operational AI use) rather than P02, which concerns default student or course stance.
units.anchor: AI tools are permitted to support decision-making, research, and operational efficiency
units.policy: AI tools are permitted to support decision-making, research, and operational efficiency.

units.why: The same overview says AI 'cannot make final personnel, disciplinary, or student decisions, which must remain human-driven', a bar on AI as sole basis for decisions about people, so P73.
units.anchor: cannot make final personnel, disciplinary, or student decisions
units.policy: AI cannot make final personnel, disciplinary, or student decisions, which must remain human-driven.

units.why: The Transparency principle sets a guiding principle for the university's AI framework (not a specific disclosure step), so P56.
units.anchor: Demanding complete and honest communication about the use, capabilities, and limitations of AI

units.why: The Academic Integrity principle states a principle of the framework without any operational rule, so P56 informs.
units.anchor: Preserving the fundamental values of intellectual honesty, original thought, and scholarly rigor

units.why: The Accessibility & Equity principle commits to inclusive, accessible tools and avoiding bias; closest type is P51 (equitable access) although it also names bias.
units.anchor: Ensuring AI tools are inclusive and accessible, avoiding bias and disproportionate impacts
units.fit_note: Also names avoiding bias and disproportionate impacts, which P51 does not capture.

units.why: The Human Oversight principle requires human involvement in 'AI-assisted decision-making processes', which is the P73 idea of keeping humans responsible for decisions.
units.anchor: All AI-assisted decision-making processes must include active human involvement and accountability

units.why: Data from AI systems 'must be handled according to the University’s Data Classification Standard and external legal and regulatory frameworks', i.e. compliance with existing standards and law: P77.
units.anchor: must be handled according to the University’s
units.frag_start: Data used and generated by AI
units.policy: Data used and generated by AI and LLM systems must be handled according to the University’s Data Classification Standard and external legal and regulatory frameworks.

units.why: Confidential and Internal data 'must be safeguarded from ... upload' to AI, a data-protection rule, so P50.
units.anchor: Confidential \Internal data must be safeguarded from unauthorized access, upload, and misuse

units.why: Entering confidential data into unauthorized AI 'is a public disclosure and must follow' the incident response program, a duty to report data exposure: P71.
units.anchor: is a public disclosure and must follow the steps defined in Oakland University’s Cyber Incident
units.policy: Entering Confidential and Internal Data into unauthorized AI systems is a public disclosure and must follow the steps defined in Oakland University’s Cyber Incident Response Program.

units.why: Before entering Confidential Data into an AI tool, users are told to 'confer with UTS first', a data-protection step: P50.
units.anchor: please confer with UTS first

units.why: Third-party tools 'must comply' with privacy laws and 'procurement must verify vendor compliance', a vendor-review rule: P65.
units.anchor: All third-party AI tools must comply with applicable data privacy laws
units.policy: All third-party AI tools must comply with applicable data privacy laws (e.g., FERPA, HIPAA, GDPR), and procurement must verify vendor compliance.

units.why: Users are 'required to pause and verify the classification of that data' before pasting into AI, a personal-data protection step: P50.
units.anchor: you are required to pause and verify the classification of that data

units.why: States AI will not be the sole basis of 'personnel, award, or disciplinary decisions': P73.
units.anchor: GenAI and LLMs will not be solely used to make personnel, award, or disciplinary decisions

units.why: A general rule that decision-making 'may not be delegated to GenAI systems', matching P73.
units.anchor: Decision-making may not be delegated to GenAI systems

units.why: The university describes a purchasing-checklist review of AI tools ('thorough evaluation ... before implementation'), an institutional vendor/tool review: P65.
units.anchor: all AI tools undergo thorough evaluation by cross-functional experts before implementation

units.why: Approved tools are re-evaluated after major updates; this extends the institutional tool review (P65) over time.
units.anchor: All approved AI systems are subject to re-evaluation upon major updates or model changes
units.fit_note: Adds periodic re-evaluation of already approved tools.

units.why: Research applications are handed to the Research Office's AI in Research Guidance, a research-use rule by deferral: P62.
units.anchor: AI In Research Guidance

units.why: For teaching, learning and academic integrity the IT guideline sets no rule and sends readers to CETL guidance. No type captures deferring a topic to another office's guidance.
units.anchor: Please refer to AI Guidance provided by the
units.uncovered_note: Defers teaching, learning and academic-integrity AI rules to the CETL guidance.

units.why: Finance and Administration may use AI for efficiency, an operational use rule: P76.
units.anchor: AI may be used for enhancing institutional efficiency, including resource optimization

units.why: AI recommendations need human review and approval before action: P73.
units.anchor: AI-generated recommendations must be reviewed and approved by appropriate human decision-makers

units.why: Planning use is allowed but AI 'must not replace human judgment': P73.
units.anchor: must not replace human judgment
units.policy: AI may support strategic planning through data modeling and predictive analytics but must not replace human judgment.

units.why: Requires monitoring to detect bias and errors in AI planning uses; closest is P53 (bias concerns), though it is a monitoring duty.
units.anchor: Ongoing performance monitoring is required to detect bias, errors, or deviations from institutional values
units.fit_note: Is a monitoring requirement, not just a naming of bias concerns.

units.why: HR may use AI for screening but AI 'may not make personnel decisions': P73.
units.anchor: may not make personnel decisions (e.g., hiring, promotion, termination)
units.policy: AI may support initial candidate screening or workload analysis but may not make personnel decisions (e.g., hiring, promotion, termination).

units.why: Requires human oversight for HR uses of AI, keeping humans responsible for decisions about people: P73.
units.anchor: All HR-related uses of AI require human oversight to prevent bias and protect employee rights

units.why: Student Affairs may use AI for registrar and financial-aid communication: administrative AI use, P76.
units.anchor: AI may enhance administrative functions such as registrar processes, financial aid communication

units.why: AI is 'prohibited from making independent enrollment or disciplinary decisions' which 'require human review': P73.
units.anchor: AI is prohibited from making independent enrollment or disciplinary decisions

units.why: Creates a governance council to oversee implementation, review incidents and evaluate technologies. No type covers setting up a governing body.
units.anchor: will establish an AI Governance Council including representatives from Academic Affairs, IT, Legal
units.uncovered_note: Establishes an AI Governance Council with named membership to oversee policy implementation.

units.why: A stated annual review cycle for the guidelines: P54.
units.anchor: These guidelines will be reviewed annually to remain current

units.why: Creates a duty to report AI misuse and concerns through the AI Incident Reporting Process: P71.
units.anchor: Any misuse, unintended consequences, or ethical concerns regarding AI must be reported

units.why: Violations 'may result in disciplinary or administrative action, as outlined in applicable university policies': violations fall under existing policies, P77.
units.anchor: Violations of these guidelines may result in disciplinary or administrative action
units.fit_note: Is the enforcement statement of the guideline; P77 is the nearest type.

units.why: Names the Chief Information Security Officer as the authority that interprets, monitors and enforces the guidelines; no type covers assigning policy ownership.
units.anchor: Primary authority for interpretation, monitoring, and enforcement of this standard
units.uncovered_note: Assigns who interprets, monitors and enforces the AI guidelines.
